body:
**Question.** When the slave port's qualified Announce carries no path trace TLV, which pathTrace does the engine publish? It currently publishes the empty sequence (count zero).

**IEEE 802.1AS-2011 (+Cor1-2013, Cor2-2015)**, the edition Milan v1.2 profiles:
- 10.3.10.2.1 d) writes pathTrace only when a path trace TLV is present: it copies pathSequence and appends thisClock.
- With no TLV there is no rule, so pathTrace keeps its previous value. That is `{thisClock}` after 10.3.12.1.1 or 10.3.12.1.4 i), or else the last trace derived from a TLV.

**IEEE 802.1AS-2020** produces the empty sequence the engine publishes today:
- 10.3.11.2.1 d) sets the port's receivedPathTrace to the empty array when no TLV is present.
- 10.3.13.2.4 f) 5) copies receivedPathTrace to pathTrace and appends thisClock only if it is not empty.

The engine therefore departs from the adopted edition in this one case. Through GET_AS_PATH (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.41.2) a controller sees count 0 where the 2011 reading gives count 1 (`{thisClock}`) or the previous trace.

**Decision needed (gPTP owner):** either align the engine to the 2011 behaviour (keep the previous pathTrace), or keep the 2020 behaviour and record why. Possible reasons: interoperability, or that the TLV is optional under 2011 and peers always send it in practice.

Found in milan-fpga PR #770 review R677-5 (issuecomment-6372618017). The behaviour is described as a cross-edition statement in milan-fpga `docs/reference/REGISTER_MAP.md` (0x7DC section). Related: #82, #85. milan-fpga #770 changes no engine behaviour.
title: pathTrace with no path trace TLV: the engine publishes the empty sequence (802.1AS-2020); 2011 keeps the previous pathTrace
